transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Thank you for calling Cymbal Telecom. My name is Chloe. How can I help you today?

transcript.speaker: User
transcript.text: Hi, yes, I need some help. I just got my bill and it's... it's over three thousand dollars! This has to be a mistake.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Oh, I can certainly understand your concern seeing a bill that high. I'll definitely look into this for you. To get started, could I please have your name?

transcript.speaker: User
transcript.text: David Gonzalez.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Thank you, David. And just to pull up your account securely, can you please confirm the phone number associated with the account?

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Perfect. And for security purposes, could you please provide me with the 4-digit security PIN on your account?

transcript.speaker: User
transcript.text: Yeah, hold on... I think it's... 5-7-4-0.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: That's correct. Thank you for verifying your information, Mr. Gonzalez. Let me just pull up your latest billing statement now.

transcript.speaker: User
transcript.text: Please do. I've never had a bill like this. My plan is supposed to be unlimited.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Okay, I see the statement here. I do see a total amount due that is significantly higher than your usual $65 monthly charge. Let me open the detailed view... one moment.

transcript.speaker: User
transcript.text: Take your time, just please tell me it's a computer glitch.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Alright, looking at the itemized charges, it appears the majority of this total is from international roaming data usage. Did you recently travel outside of the country?

transcript.speaker: User
transcript.text: Yes! I was in Portugal for about ten days. But my plan is unlimited! Why would I be charged for data?

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: I understand the confusion. Your Cymbal Unlimited 5G Mobile Plan provides unlimited data, talk, and text within the United States, and also includes Canada and Mexico. However, for travel to other countries like Portugal, standard international roaming rates apply unless an international package is added.

transcript.speaker: User
transcript.text: Nobody told me that! That's completely misleading. Why call it 'unlimited' then?

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: I can see why it would feel that way. The 'unlimited' refers to the quantity of data, not the geographic area. Our system shows that upon arrival in Portugal, we sent a standard welcome SMS to your device outlining the pay-per-use rates, which are $0.25 per minute for calls and $2.05 per megabyte for data.

transcript.speaker: User
transcript.text: A text message? I get dozens of spam texts a day! I might have seen it, I don't know, I didn't think it would lead to a three-thousand-dollar bill! A megabyte? What even is that? That's nothing!

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: You're right, a megabyte is a small amount of data on its own. However, modern smartphone apps, especially things like maps, social media, and video, can use hundreds of megabytes very quickly.

transcript.speaker: User
transcript.text: So what am I supposed to do? Not use my phone when I travel?

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Let me look at the specific usage. I see a large block of data was used on June 12th... around 1.5 gigabytes. Do you recall what you might have been doing on your phone then?

transcript.speaker: User
transcript.text: June 12th... we were driving from Lisbon to Algarve. I was using my phone for GPS navigation for a few hours. That's it!

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: That would explain it. GPS navigation apps can consume a significant amount of data continuously. To give you some perspective, 1.5 gigabytes is equivalent to 1,536 megabytes.

transcript.speaker: User
transcript.text: Okay... and?

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Well, at the standard rate of $2.05 per megabyte... just for that one period of usage, the charge would be over $3,100.

transcript.speaker: User
transcript.text: What? That's... that's insane. That's more than my flight and hotel. I cannot pay that. I will not pay that. This is extortion.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: I truly do understand your shock, Mr. Gonzalez, and I want to help you with this. Let me review your account history. Please allow me to place you on a brief hold for about 60 seconds while I check for any available options.

transcript.speaker: User
transcript.text: Fine. But if you come back and tell me I have to pay this, I'm switching carriers tomorrow. I swear.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: I understand. One moment please.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Thank you for your patience, Mr. Gonzalez.

transcript.speaker: User
transcript.text: Yeah. What did you find?

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Okay, so I've reviewed your account details. I can see that you've been a loyal Cymbal Telecom customer for six years, and you've always had a perfect payment history. We really value you as a customer.

transcript.speaker: User
transcript.text: Okay... so?

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: So, while the charges are technically valid based on the terms of service, I've spoken with my supervisor given the circumstances and your customer history. We want to work with you on this.

transcript.speaker: User
transcript.text: I'm listening.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Cymbal Telecom offers an International Day Pass, which is a feature customers can add for travel. It provides full use of your domestic plan's talk, text, and data allowances in over 200 countries for a flat fee of $10 per 24-hour period.

transcript.speaker: User
transcript.text: So for ten bucks a day I could have used my phone normally?

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Exactly. You only get charged for the days you actually use service abroad.

transcript.speaker: User
transcript.text: Why wasn't I offered this before I left? Or when I called to say I was traveling?

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: That's a very fair question. I don't see any notes on your account of you notifying us of your travel dates beforehand. Typically, we advise customers on these options if they call in to let us know they'll be abroad.

transcript.speaker: User
transcript.text: I didn't know I had to. I've traveled before and just used Wi-Fi. This time I needed navigation.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: I completely understand. Here is what I am able to do for you. As a one-time courtesy, I can retroactively apply the International Day Pass to your account for the days you incurred roaming charges in Portugal.

transcript.speaker: User
transcript.text: You can do that? Backwards?

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Yes. Let me check the exact dates of usage. It looks like your phone connected to our partner network in Portugal for a total of 9 days during your trip.

transcript.speaker: User
transcript.text: Okay, so 9 days.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: That's right. So, instead of the pay-per-use data charges, your bill would be adjusted to reflect 9 days of the International Day Pass. That's 9 days times $10 per day.

transcript.speaker: User
transcript.text: So... ninety dollars? Instead of over three thousand?

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: That is correct. We would remove the roaming data charge of $3,145.70 and replace it with a charge of $90 for the Day Passes.

transcript.speaker: User
transcript.text: Yes! Oh my god, yes. Please, absolutely, do that. Thank you.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: You're very welcome. I'm happy we could find a solution for you. Let me go ahead and process that adjustment right now.

transcript.speaker: User
transcript.text: Wow. Okay, thank you. I was really panicking there for a minute.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: I can only imagine. Just give me one moment while I apply this credit and adjustment to the billing system... it takes a few clicks to get it all confirmed.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Alright, the adjustment has been submitted. I have a reference number for you for today's call and the changes made. It's 8-4-2-1-B.

transcript.speaker: User
transcript.text: 8-4-2-1-B. Got it. So what happens now with the bill I see online?

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: That's a great question. It can take 24 to 48 hours for the system to update the total amount due that you see in your online portal. However, I've placed a note on your account and confirmed the adjustment. The correct total for this billing cycle will be your standard $65 plan, plus the $90 for the Day Passes, plus your usual taxes and fees.

transcript.speaker: User
transcript.text: So around one hundred and fifty-five dollars, plus tax.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Exactly. You can disregard the previous total. When your automatic payment runs, it will draft the corrected, lower amount.

transcript.speaker: User
transcript.text: That is such a relief. Chloe, thank you so much. You've been incredibly helpful.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: It's my pleasure, Mr. Gonzalez. And for future reference, you can easily activate the International Day Pass yourself right from the Cymbal Telecom mobile app before you travel. It's under the 'International' section in 'Plan & Add-ons'.

transcript.speaker: User
transcript.text: Okay, I will definitely remember that for next time. The app, got it.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Is there anything else I can assist you with today? Perhaps questions about your plan or any other services?

transcript.speaker: User
transcript.text: No, that was the only thing. You've solved my huge problem, and I really appreciate it.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: I'm very glad to hear that. We appreciate your business and thank you for being a Cymbal Telecom customer.

transcript.speaker: User
transcript.text: Thanks again, Chloe.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: You're welcome. Thank you for calling Cymbal Telecom. Have a wonderful rest of your day.

transcript.speaker: User
transcript.text: You too. Bye.
